decisionGroups.title: VAT ID for a client you sold to tax-free
decisionGroups.why: These sales were booked without German VAT as intra-EU supplies. That needs a valid VAT ID. Without one, they may be taxable in Germany.

decisionGroups.title: Client without a country
decisionGroups.why: The country decides whether German VAT applies. Some of this client's invoices are in US dollars and carry German VAT.

decisionGroups.title: Possible duplicate client
decisionGroups.why: Two client records share name, VAT ID, IBAN and e-mail. Merging keeps one record and the history of both.

decisionGroups.title: Costs to place
decisionGroups.why: The model was not sure which expense account these freelancer and vendor bills belong to. The account decides which line of your profit and loss they appear on.

decisionGroups.title: Money in that matches no invoice
decisionGroups.why: Payments arrived that the engine could not link to an invoice. They can stay unassigned for now; your tax advisor will see them.

decisionGroups.title: Money out to clients with no credit note
decisionGroups.why: Payments went out to clients without a matching credit note. None of the amounts equals an open credit note exactly.

decisionGroups.title: Clients who paid slightly too much
decisionGroups.why: The extra amounts are small. Keeping them as credit for the client's next invoice is the usual choice.

decisionGroups.title: German client with a malformed VAT ID
decisionGroups.why: Their invoices carry German VAT, so the tax treatment does not change. The client record should still be corrected.

decisionGroups.title: One-cent rounding differences
decisionGroups.why: The old system's gross amount was one cent off net plus VAT, on sales and supplier invoices. Compare it with what was actually paid before choosing.

$comment: CONFIG-ONLY DEMO. Reuses Nordlicht's engine output (no second dataset was provided) to show what configuration alone changes: words, people, roles, order and wording of decision groups.
